newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-BIG SERVERS TRIUMPH AT QUEEN'S.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BIG SERVERS TRIUMPH AT QUEEN'S.

text.p: Big serves triumphed at Queen's on Friday with Mark Philippoussis of Australia and Britain's Greg Rusedski taking full advantage of the fast surface to book places in the London Grass Court Championship semifinals.
Philippoussis, ranked 19th in the world, dismissed Germany's Jens Knippschild, a lowly 105, 6-2 6-7 6-4 without really raising his game.
"I never felt concerned. I never looked like losing my serve," the 20-year-old Philippoussis, who has served 63 aces in four matches so far this tournament, said.
"He played a really good tie-break, but I was always comfortable."
The tall brooding Australian, who has won tournaments in Munich and Scottsdale this year, holds the record for the fastest ever recorded serve in tennis at 229 kph.
He said the tournament was proving fine preparation for Wimbledon in 10 days' time. "I'm playing great at the moment and I always feel comfortable on grass. I'm looking forward to it," he said.
Rusedski became the first British player ever to reach the semifinals at Queen's, beating French Open semifinalist Patrick Rafter 4-6 7-5 6-3.
The big-hitting Canadian-born Briton, seeded 16 and ranked 44th in the world, had to raise and tighten his game after a series of volleying errors in the first set.
"Pat looked tired after his long run at the French," Rusedski said. "And midway though the second set I started playing some of the best tennis I've played so far this year.
"I can still make progress -- my volleying could be sharper, but I'm pleased with my progress," he said.
